question: The word _____ in the Preamble to the Constitution of India implies an 'elected Head of the State'.
solution:
The correct answer is __**republic.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Preamble** to the Constitution of India starts with the words "**We, the people of India"**.
 
• This implies that the people of India are the** ultimate source of power** in the country.
 
• The Preamble declares India to be a "s**overeign, socialist, secular, democratic republic".**
 
• Each of these words has a** specific meaning.**
 
• India is a republic because it has an **elected head of state.**
 
• The **President **of India is elected by an **Electoral College** consisting of the elected members of both **houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies** of the States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sovereign:** India is a **free country** and has the power to govern itself without any external interference.
 
• **Socialist:** The Indian government is committed to creating a society where there is **social and economic equality** for all.
 
• **Secular: **India **does not **have an official state religion and all religions are treated equally.
 
• **Democratic: **The people of India have the right to **elect their representatives** and participate in the **democratic process.**
